claims.statement: The `wiki-update` Nx target on the `infrastructure-as-code` project runs `node scripts/wiki-generate.mjs`, which resolves the model provider and spawns `openwiki code --update --print`; the target's own `env` block supplies the telemetry opt-out (`OPENWIKI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`), the raised Node heap (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`) and an explicit per-turn output cap, so a bare `openwiki` invocation reintroduces the OOM and the silent zero-page failure.

`OPENWIKI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=16384` is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: an unset or too-small per-turn cap truncates a turn before it opens a tool call, which is the model loop's stop condition, so the generator exits 0 having written nothing; `scripts/wiki-generate.mjs` refuses to start below 16384 and `scripts/__tests__/wiki-maintain.guard.test.mjs` fails an unset or too-small cap, a model id the generator's own resolver does not match, and any id that would land on the legacy 4096 fallback.

A wiki run message is scoped by passing it as a single argv element from `WIKI_RUN_MESSAGE`, never via `nx --args`, which strips its quoting and leaves the run unscoped; `wiki-generate.mjs` rejects every argument other than `--preflight` so an unrecognised flag can never mean 'start a paid run', and it invokes the generator with `--update` so the interactive `--init` onboarding is avoided.

`pnpm nx okf-lint infrastructure-as-code` runs `scripts/check-openwiki-okf.mjs`, the OKF conformance gate over the `openwiki/` bundle (front matter parses, required `type`, ISO-8601 stamps, repo-relative `resource` links resolving, an `index.md` per directory, no orphaned concepts), and `pnpm nx okf-governance infrastructure-as-code` runs the separate governance gate `scripts/check-openwiki-governance.mjs` over the regeneration policy, protection fingerprints and index.

Both OpenWiki gates are offline and keyless by construction — external `resource` links and body links are shape-checked and resolved against the working tree, never fetched — so the always-on guardrails job cannot fail because a third-party host is down; each gate's `--selftest` runs first in CI so a rule that silently stopped detecting its case turns the build red.

Both gates are fail-closed with deliberately no skip flag and no allowlist: an absent, empty or partially-written bundle is a violation rather than a vacuous pass, and a rejected page is fixed in `openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md` and regenerated rather than accepted in place — because an allowlisted leak stays leaked.

The conformance gate's rules V14 and V15 check body links rather than front matter: V14 rejects a site-root-absolute link (a leading `/` resolves against the forge's site root and 404s) and V15 rejects a relative link that does not resolve from its own file's directory; links inside a code fence or code span are exempt, and V14's finding names the relative form to write instead.

Drift detection (V12) is report-only: a concept whose cited source's last commit date is newer than its stamp produces a warning that never affects the exit code, and it is not an input to the planner — `planSlices` takes only the paths changed since the run-record marker plus the carried-forward backlog, so a concept whose source moved before the marker is not re-planned automatically.

A concept that cites a `resource` but carries no usable stamp is counted and printed by the gate rather than silently skipped — it is not a conformance violation and never fails the build, but the counter makes a silent loss of drift coverage visible.

The concept provenance stamp is the NEWEST of `generated.at`, `verified.at` and `timestamp`, defined once in `scripts/openwiki-stamp.mjs` and imported by both the gate's V12 drift warning and the maintenance run's stale-page check, so the two readers cannot resolve the same page to different dates.

`wiki-maintain` judges a slice by the pages that actually landed in the working tree, by bundle conformance and by whether policy permitted every written path — never by the generator's exit status, because the generator was measured exiting 0 after twelve minutes of paid work that wrote a single `index.md`.

Maintenance exit codes are distinguishable and a budget stop is not a failure: `1` is a slice that failed verification, `2` is bad usage, an unreadable record or a missing credential, and `3` is a run stopped at the page or wall-clock budget with work carried forward — the workflow and the orchestrator both report 0 and 3 as 'nothing is broken'.

The maintenance budgets are page and wall-clock only and are explicitly NOT monetary bounds (the generator reports no token or cost data); the values are constants in `scripts/wiki-maintain.mjs` and a guard test derives the CI job's `timeout-minutes` from them, so changing one without the other fails offline.

`wiki-plan` is the free, offline planning target that decomposes documentation changes since the last recorded run into bounded slices of at most 8 pages and exactly one bundle area, so a paid run is reviewable before it happens; `wiki-maintain` is the paid execution path around it.

Freshness is event-driven rather than periodic: on a feature branch the wiki refresh is folded into the feature-completion checklist (`pnpm nx wiki-update infrastructure-as-code`, then `okf-lint`, both part of completing the feature), and on `main` it comes from the merge-triggered `.forgejo/workflows/wiki-maintain.yml`, which has no `schedule:` trigger and starts a run only after `main` has been quiet for about fifteen minutes via concurrency plus cancel-in-progress plus an initial sleep.
The wiki-maintenance job is deliberately never a required CI context, because it is paid and occasionally slow and must not gate an unrelated merge.

The generation brief `openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md` and the regeneration policy `openwiki/policy.yaml` are hand-authored and declared `never-written`: the brief is read on every run but never rewritten and is the sole remediation surface when a gate rejects generated content, and the policy file's own policy is `never-written` so the process it constrains cannot rewrite it.

A durable learning goes to the canonical home of its subject, decided mechanically from the concept covering it: a concept carrying a `resource` cites an upstream source, so the learning goes to that source; a concept with no upstream source is authoritative and the learning goes into the concept itself; the governance gate enforces that every concept is provably exactly one of the two, because the routing rule is undecidable otherwise.

Protected passages may only be attached to authoritative concepts (fingerprinting a derived summary would freeze it against the document it summarizes), and to change one legitimately its text and its fingerprint must be updated in the same change via `node scripts/check-openwiki-governance.mjs --fingerprint openwiki/<area>/<page>.md "<anchor>"` — the manifest is the authority, so a listed passage that no longer appears fails as a removal rather than as nothing-to-compare.

`docs/proposals/**` is deliberately excluded from the bundle as pre-specification ideation superseded the moment a spec exists; exactly one `type: Process` concept describes the proposal → spec → implementation lifecycle and links to the folder for humans who want the history, while the runbooks that were relocated out of the proposal tree are in scope.

Mermaid diagram generation degrades silently without its parser: `mermaid` and `jsdom` are optional peer dependencies of the generator, and without them a fence that fails the strict post-run validation is rewritten in place into a plain `text` fence while the run still exits 0 and every gate still passes — so both are installed beside the generator in the toolchain image and in the wiki workflow, and a guard test asserts the two lists match.

The maintenance run normalizes body links deterministically after each slice — rewriting only the target inside `](…)` to the file-relative form and skipping code fences and spans — while the conformance gate's V14/V15 remain the fail-closed backstop for a link that arrives by another route.
